meta.title: Otto — Autonomous work agent
meta.description: Give Otto a goal in plain language. It plans, calls tools across your workspace, and shows every step it takes.

landing.heroSubtitle: Otto plans and executes multi-step tasks by calling tools across a real workspace of contacts, deals, tasks, and documents. Every step it takes is shown in a live trace, so you always see what it did and why.
landing.heroNote: No signup. One click loads a seeded workspace.
landing.trustLine: One goal in. A plan, a sequence of tool calls, and a result out.
landing.featuresTitle: An agent you can actually watch
landing.featuresSubtitle: Otto is transparent by design. Nothing is hidden behind a single black-box answer.
landing.feature1Body: Otto queries records, searches the knowledge base, drafts emails, creates tasks, and updates deals. Every action changes real data you can inspect.
landing.feature2Body: Each step shows Otto's thought, the tool it called with exact arguments, and the observation it got back before deciding what to do next.
landing.feature3Body: Otto only acts on data the tools return. Arithmetic runs on a real calculator, not the model, so the numbers are exact.
landing.feature4Body: Every run has a step limit, a daily cap, and a sandbox that keeps Otto inside your own workspace.
landing.how1Body: Describe what you want done in plain language, or pick one of the example goals.
landing.how2Body: It calls one tool at a time, reads each result, and decides the next step, streaming everything live.
landing.how3Body: Otto finishes with a clear summary, and every draft, task, and update lands in your workspace.
landing.toolsSubtitle: Otto composes these tools to accomplish a goal.
landing.ctaTitle: See Otto run in under a minute
landing.ctaBody: Load the seeded demo workspace and give Otto a goal.
landing.footerNote: Otto is a portfolio demo. Data is seeded and no email is ever actually sent.

dashboard.composerPlaceholder: Describe a goal, e.g. Find my top overdue deals and draft a follow-up for each.
examples: Find my top 3 overdue deals, draft a short follow-up email for each contact, and create a task to review them next week.
Which contacts have had no activity in 30 days? Draft a re-engagement email for each and add a note to their record.
Summarize the refund policy, then add a note about it to every enterprise contact.
Total the open pipeline for enterprise deals and create a task to prepare a forecast review.
